Each arc gets a phase of a quarter turn, so the cell for A, B is -0.5i (accent) and its mirror B, A is the conjugate 0.5i (teal), and likewise around the cycle; the diagonal holds the degree 1. The matrix is Hermitian and records the direction of every arc." width="100%"} The magnetic Laplacian (Fanuel et al., 2018) encodes edge direction as a complex phase, like the potential of a magnetic field acting on a charged particle walking the graph. A one-way edge $j \to k$ contributes $e^{2\pi i q}$ to entry $(j, k)$ and its conjugate to $(k, j)$, so the matrix is Hermitian: its eigenvalues are real and its eigenvectors give "magnetic eigenmaps", spectral embeddings of directed graphs that place nodes in the order of the flow, revealing cycles and hierarchies that the symmetrized Laplacian loses. The charge `q` sets how strongly direction counts; at `q = 0` this is the Laplacian of the graph with directions ignored (and two-way edges counted once, with the mean weight). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [q]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.25]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The charge, between `0` and `0.5`. Default is `0.25`, where a one-way edge's phase is a quarter turn, $i$. [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to return the normalized magnetic Laplacian $I - D^{-1/2} H D^{-1/2}$ instead of $D - H$. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[list[list[complex]], list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(matrix, node_ids)`: the Hermitian matrix as a list of rows of `complex` values, and the node IDs labelling rows and columns, in increasing order. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected or `q` is not between `0` and `0.5`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} With $W$ the weighted adjacency matrix and $W' = (W + W^T) / 2$, the Hermitian adjacency matrix is $H_{jk} = W'_{jk} e^{2\pi i q \delta_{jk}}$, where $\delta_{jk}$ is $+1$ if only $j \to k$ is an edge, $-1$ if only $k \to j$ is, and $0$ if both are. $D$ is diagonal with the row sums of $|H|$, that is of $W'$. Self-loops are left out. In the normalized form, isolated nodes get zero rows apart from the 1 on the diagonal. Matches NetworkX's `magnetic_laplacian_matrix()`; NetworkX rejects multigraphs, while parallel edges add their weights here. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A directed triangle: each one-way edge gives the phase $\pm i$ at the default `q = 0.25`: ::: {#27eb6965 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec cycle = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) cycle.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A")]) matrix, nodes = cycle.magnetic_laplacian_matrix() [[complex(round(z.real, 3) + 0.0, round(z.imag, 3) + 0.0) for z in row] for row in matrix] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [[(1+0j), -0.5j, 0.5j], [0.5j, (1+0j), -0.5j], [-0.5j, 0.5j, (1+0j)]] ``` ::: :::
